records.name: Slow Food Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the Slow Food movement. It runs social and learning dinners and gives a Snail of Approval award to local food businesses that meet its standards for good, clean, and fair food.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a chapter dinner, such as the banquet on October 22, 2026 in Queen Village. Join as a member to get the chapter's seasonal recipes, or volunteer through the get involved pages.

schedule.text: Chapter dinners and events, posted on the website as they are planned. The next one listed is a banquet on Thursday, October 22, 2026, 6 to 9 pm.

locations.label: Queen Village (venue address not on the event page)

cost.text: $30 per adult ticket for the October 22, 2026 banquet. $5 of each ticket goes to the chapter. The event page also shows a Free label in one place, which conflicts.

first_step.how: Register through the register button on the banquet's event page, or use the join page to become a member
first_step.basis: Public ticketed events with a clear register button and a membership page; the page does not say that beginners are specifically welcome

records.notes: The homepage says no events are scheduled but also lists this banquet, so the page is inconsistent. Membership fee and benefits beyond recipes were not checked.

records.name: Weavers Way Environment Committee
records.summary: A member-run committee of the Weavers Way food co-op that looks into environmental issues, plans green projects, and gives grants to community groups. It meets most months.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly meeting, help research local environmental issues, and help plan green projects and the grant decisions.

schedule.text: Meets on the second Wednesday of the month at 7 pm. The 2026 list has no meetings in July or August. January and February meetings are virtual. The October 14, 2026 meeting is at Springfield Library in Wyndmoor.

locations.label: Rotating meeting places: Ambler, Wyndmoor and Springfield (Montgomery County), and a Germantown site

cost.text: No fee is listed for meetings

first_step.how: Email environment@weaversway.coop to be put on the list. The January and February virtual meetings need an email to be included.
first_step.basis: Only Weavers Way members can join, and the page asks people to email first, so the way in is not open to everyone

records.notes: Most meetings are outside Philadelphia, in Montgomery County, but the co-op serves Philadelphia members. The co-op's working membership rules are not recorded here as a group.

records.name: Plastic Reduction Task Force (Weavers Way)
records.summary: A task force under the Weavers Way Environment Committee. It studies plastic waste across its life cycle and advises the co-op on cutting single-use plastics.
records.what_you_do: Help with the task force's work on plastic waste and raise awareness among members. Email the task force to ask how to take part.

first_step.basis: Listed as a Weavers Way member group with an email address; membership comes first and meeting details are not published

records.notes: Thin record: the committees page gives the purpose and an email but no meeting times or dated items for this task force. Status is probably active because the committees page is current, but no dated evidence was found for this task force alone.

records.name: Weavers Way Emergency Response Network (WERN)
records.summary: A newly formed network of Weavers Way members who set up small neighborhood groups, called pods, to look out for one another in an emergency. It also shares preparedness tips.
records.what_you_do: Join or help start a neighborhood pod, learn preparedness basics at the monthly meeting, or help organize in your area.

schedule.text: Meets monthly at Summit Church in Mt. Airy. The page gives no meeting dates or year.

first_step.how: Ask the co-op's Membership Department at member@weaversway.coop how to join a pod or attend a monthly meeting
first_step.basis: Membership comes first, and the page's own contact addresses look malformed, so the way in is unclear

records.notes: Newly formed per the page, with no dates. The two email addresses on the page (preparedness@weaverswaycoop and prepardness@weaversway.coop) are both malformed, so no group email is recorded. Verify with the Membership Department before sharing. The Membership Department address above is the co-op's general member contact, not the network's.

records.name: Homebrewers of Philadelphia and Suburbs (HOPS)
records.summary: A homebrewing club for beer makers in the Philadelphia area and its suburbs. It meets monthly to talk about brewing methods and beer styles, and it runs a yearly homebrew competition called HOPS BOPS.
records.what_you_do: Come to a meeting to hear about brewing, watch demonstrations, and taste beers. Members can enter the HOPS BOPS competition.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings on the third Thursday, about 6 to 8 pm, usually at Home Sweet Homebrew and sometimes at BYOB restaurants. The page says times vary.

cost.text: Dues are not published on the club site

first_step.how: Email the club contact named on the club site to ask about membership and whether guests can come to a meeting
first_step.basis: The site does not say whether guests can attend, and the only route it lists is an email

records.notes: Status is dormant on purpose: the newest dated item on the club site is a HOPS BOPS 2019 results page, and the site footer reads 2014. The club may still meet. The meeting venue, Home Sweet Homebrew, was not checked for a Philadelphia address. Ask the club before listing a meeting. The club's Facebook group and mailing list were seen as links only and were not read.

records.name: Sankofa Community Farm Volunteer Days (Bartram's Garden)
records.summary: Volunteer work days on the Sankofa Community Farm at Bartram's Garden in Southwest Philadelphia. Volunteers help plant, harvest, weed, pull invasive plants, and care for the orchard alongside farm staff.
records.what_you_do: Arrive at 9:30 am for a short safety briefing, then work outdoors with farm staff on planting, harvesting, weeding, and orchard care for about two and a half hours.

schedule.text: Saturday volunteer days from 9:30 am to 12 pm. The published dates are October 10, October 24 and November 14, 2026.

locations.label: Sankofa Community Farm at Bartram's Garden

first_step.how: Sign up for a listed volunteer day through its Learn More link on the venue page. Each person registers alone to complete the volunteer waiver.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says no special skills or past experience are needed, and it explains how to register

records.notes: Bartram's Garden also belongs to the gardens list, so this may merge with a garden record. The Horticulture Volunteer Day on October 17 is not a farm day and is not recorded. Age rules are published only for Welcome Volunteers (18 and over, minors with a parent), not for farm days. The phone is the garden's general line, not a farm line.

leads_only.note: Nonprofit arm of the co-op working on healthy food access, linked from the co-op's community page. Volunteer roles and events not checked.

leads_only.note: The farm pages linked as Our Farms could not be reached: weaversway.coop/farms returned an image and /our-farms returned 404. The calendar lists farm market events and a class at the Henry Avenue market, but no farm volunteer days.

leads_only.note: The homepage links a Working Membership page and a Governance page. The guessed working-membership address returned 404, so shift types and any member committees were not verified. The join page gives a $200 equity payment, which is not recorded as a group.

notes: Searches: all 3 used (budget exhausted). Fetches: 26. Published 6 records: Slow Food Philadelphia (banquet on Oct 22, 2026); Weavers Way Environment Committee; Weavers Way Plastic Reduction Task Force; Weavers Way Emergency Response Network (low confidence, no dates); Homebrewers of Philadelphia and Suburbs (dormant, low confidence, newest dated item is 2019); Sankofa Community Farm volunteer days at Bartram's Garden (Oct 10, Oct 24 and Nov 14, 2026, all shown with year on the venue page). GAPS: no community supper clubs with open seats and no heritage cooking groups were found; search budget ran out before I could look for them. Community cooking classes: The Food Trust's pages listed no dated public classes (Cooking Matters is only through a partner portal). Greensgrow did not resolve (greensgrowphilly.org, greensgrowfarms.org) and greensgrow.org returned 404, so it is not recorded. Two homebrew clubs are out of area and not recorded: BUZZ (West Chester, per a 2016-era article) and Bruclear (Pottstown). Weavers Way working membership is a co-op obligation (each household member over 16 owes six hours a year), not a group, so not recorded; the co-op's fall 2026 general membership meeting on Oct 21 is also a co-op event, not a group. Dated items older than 2026 were used only for status, and footer years (2014, 2017) were not treated as evidence. Mariposa has no member committee or cooking class on the pages I could read.
